name: Fort
overview: The biblical concept of a fort encompasses both physical and figurative protections. In the Old Testament, forts and bulwarks were constructed as field fortifications and city defenses, as seen in the instructions to besiege cities without destroying fruit trees (Deuteronomy 20:19-20) and the use of caves and strongholds for refuge during times of oppression (Judges 6:2). More profoundly, Scripture portrays God Himself as the ultimate fortress—our rock, shield, high tower, and deliverer—emphasizing His protective care over His people (2 Samuel 22:2-3; Psalms 18:2). This dual imagery highlights fortifications as both tangible defenses and powerful symbols of God’s safeguarding presence.
